resume: Six-voice polysynth after the Roland JUNO-60: one DCO per voice (saw, pulse, sub, noise), resonant low-pass filter, one ADSR envelope, LFO and chorus. Arpeggiator, 16-step sequencer and 56 memories.

commandes.role: Keyboard one octave down. With OCT+: panic, all notes off, sequence and recording stopped.
Keyboard one octave up. With OCT-: panic.
CHORUS page: CHORUS (OFF, I, II, I+II), MODE (POLY, UNISON, SOLO), PORTA, SPREAD.
VCF page: CUTOFF, RES, ENV, KEYS; again, the second half: HPF, ENV (NORMAL or INVERT), VCA, LEVEL.
ENVELOPE page: ATTACK, DECAY, SUSTAIN, RELEASE, shared by the filter and the volume.
LFO page: RATE, DELAY, TO DCO, TO VCF.
DCO page: SAW, PULSE, SUB, NOISE; again, the second half: RANGE, PW, PWM.
GLOBAL page: TUNE, VELOCITY, ARP, OCTAVES; again, the second half: TEMPO, THEME, LINK.
SOUND page: sound name, mode, arp, hold and sequencer state, 16-step pattern; there K1 to K4 set CUTOFF, RES, ATTACK, RELEASE.
Keeps the sound, the settings and the pattern; lit while something has changed.
Arpeggiator on or off; while recording, inserts a rest.
Starts or stops the pattern in a loop (EMPTY: REC if there is none); starting it turns the arpeggiator off.
Hold: notes keep sounding after the keys are released; again to let go.
Starts recording and clears the old pattern: play up to 16 notes, ARP for a rest; REC again to finish.
Flips between a page's two halves.
Previous or next memory (56: 16 factory sounds, the rest INIT).
The 27-key keyboard; pressing harder makes the note louder and adds a little vibrato.

a_savoir: J6 keeps only its own data: its 56 memories, its settings and its pattern.
